title: PNDP-Manifolds for Dummies
content: Partially Negative Dimensional Product manifolds, abbreviated PNDP-manifolds, are a recently proposed class of geometric objects constructed from Einstein warped products in which the fiber is allowed to possess a virtual, or derived, negative dimension. The original construction was introduced by Pigazzini, Özel, Linker and Jafari [1]. The purpose of this paper is not to develop the most general theory of PNDP-manifolds, but to explain the basic ideas in an accessible way. We begin with ordinary manifolds, products, warped products and Einstein manifolds. We then explain why the phrase “negative dimension” should be interpreted carefully: it is not the dimension of an ordinary smooth manifold in the classical sense. Rather, it is a virtual dimension arising naturally in derived-geometric or obstruction-theoretic descriptions. We introduce the basic PNDP construction, derive its dimension formula, discuss the important zero-dimensional or “point-like” case, and give elementary examples. Finally, we explain how PNDP geometry is related to hidden dimensions, desuspension, Einstein geometry and possible applications. The paper is intended as a pedagogical introduction for readers who know elementary differential geometry but have never encountered PNDP geometry.
